newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank says CPI goal not to be undershot.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank says CPI goal not to be undershot.

text.p: Governor of Sweden's central bank, Urban Backstrom, said on Friday that the bank could undershoot its two percent inflation target given certain circumstances but that the bank did not believe it would happen.

"In the most recent months the monthly figures for the CPI (Consumer Price Index) do imply that underlying inflation has moved down to around one percent," Backstrom said at a domestic seminar on shares and finances.

"Were it to go on falling and then remain low in an 'annual perspective' one could indeed talk of the level being short of the target in the intended sense. But neither the Riksbank nor any other observer believes this will happen."
The Riksbank aims to have inflation of two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.
Backstrom also said that growth may be more stable than previously in Sweden as the economy has been expanding at a higher average overall rate than in the period of inflation in the 1970s and 1980s.
He dismissed last year's slowdown as temporary, saying this was not unusual when firms made cyclical stock adjustments.
"This year and in 1998 most of the signs point to a renewed increase in growth," Backstrom said.

"There is a possibility that growth in the future will display more longterm stability than we have been accustomed to. That too is a characteristic of a low inflation economy founded on a disciplined economic policy."
